previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. Thompson, a right-handed male with composite Hodgkin's and non-Hodgkin's lymphoma with CNS involvement, was admitted for his fifth maintenance cycle of high-dose methotrexate chemotherapy. He reported stable symptoms, primarily intermittent visual floaters that typically improve post-treatment. He tolerated the infusion well, with mild nausea managed by ondansetron. Constipation developed during admission and responded to lactulose and stool softeners. His methotrexate level decreased to 0.22, and renal function remained stable with adequate hydration and urine alkalinization. A brain MRI showed no evidence of tumor recurrence, with a small T2-hyperintense frontal lesion unchanged and consistent with gliosis. He was discharged home in stable condition on oral leucovorin, docusate, senna, and ondansetron as needed, with instructions to restart aspirin and follow up for his next chemotherapy cycle.

TECHNIQUE:  Sagittal T1 pre- and post-contrast as well as axial T1 pre- and
post-contrast, T2, FLAIR, GRE, and diffusion-weighted images were obtained.

FINDINGS:  There has been no significant change since ___.  No
evidence of mass, mass effect, or infarction.  No diffusion abnormality or
abnormal enhancement.  The small T2 hyperintense focus in the left posterior
frontal lobe with tiny areas of susceptibility consistent with old blood
products from prior biopsy is unchanged compared to the prior exam.  Left
parietal burr hole is also unchanged.  Scattered foci of white matter FLAIR
signal hyperintensities are unchanged consistent with chronic small vessel
ischemic disease.

IMPRESSION:  Unchanged T2 hyperintensity in the left posterior frontal lobe,
likely representing gliosis.  No abnormal enhancement or new foci of
hemorrhage or infarct.
